_README: Trade and industry bodies worth one short note asking for a conversation.
WHAT THIS IS NOT
Not a job application - these bodies do not hire technicians, and an
email treating them as an employer wastes the one approach we get.
Not a funding ask - see data/funding_opportunities.json for why money
is never mentioned in a cold email in this project.
It asks for a short conversation about the sector, and nothing else.
The value of a trade body is that it knows who is hiring, who is
growing, and which employers in the region take service leavers - none
of which is a favour to ask, and all of which is what they exist for.
THE RULES, SAME AS EVERYWHERE ELSE HERE
- One approach per body, ever. No follow-up sequence. A body that has
not replied has answered.
- No address is ever guessed. The name and website here are the input;
the pipeline's ordinary discovery finds a real, MX-checked address or
this sends nothing at all. No named contact is recorded here, because
inventing one would be exactly the guessing this project forbids.
- No CV attached. A CV is a job-application artifact and attaching one
to a 'could we talk' note turns it into the job pitch it is not.
VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING
Domains were correct when written. Anything marked "confidence":
"check" is one to look at before assuming the letter landed anywhere
useful.

targets.name: Global Underwater Hub
targets.note: The industry-backed body for UK underwater engineering and technology, headquartered in Aberdeen. Formed out of Subsea UK, so this is the live organisation rather than the older name.

targets.name: Society for Underwater Technology
targets.note: The professional body for underwater engineering and science, with an active Aberdeen branch running talks and evening events - the kind of room where a technician meets the people who run the work.

targets.name: Offshore Energies UK
targets.note: The trade association for the UK offshore energy industry, Aberdeen-based. Their members are the operators and contractors this whole search is aimed at.
